message.content:
**Herb‑Roasted Whole Chickens – A Simple Batch Recipe for Five**

> *This version works whether your kitchen has enough room for all five birds at once or you’ll have to split into two small batches.*

---

### Ingredients  
| Item | Quantity |
|------|----------|
| Whole chickens | **5** (≈ 3–4 lb / 1.4–1.8 kg each) |
| Extra‑virgin olive oil | ¼ cup (plus more for rubbing) |
| Kosher salt | 2 tsp (inside & outside) |
| Coarse black pepper | 1½ tsp |
| Garlic cloves | 12–16, peeled & finely minced |
| Fresh rosemary | 10 sprigs |
| Fresh thyme | 10 sprigs |
| Lemons | 5 (cut in half) |
| Onion wedges (optional) | 5 |
| Carrots & baby potatoes (optional) | Enough to fill pans |

*Feel free to swap out herbs—tarragon, sage, or oregano work great too!*

---

### Equipment  

- Oven capable of holding one or two 9×13″ sheets/racks  
- Roasting rack(s) or sturdy wire mesh  
- Meat thermometer (instant-read)

---

### Instructions  

#### 1️⃣ Prep the Birds  
1. Remove giblets from cavities (save for stock if desired).  
2. Pat each bird dry with paper towels – crisp skin starts with dryness.  
3. Season generously inside & out with salt & pepper.  

#### 2️⃣ Flavor Boosters  
1. Mix ⅓ cup olive oil with minced garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme, and zest of one lemon.  
2. Loosen the skin over the breast area gently with fingertips; rub this herb mixture under the skin for maximum flavor penetration.  
3. Stuff each cavity with ½ lemon wedge + 2 sprigs of rosemary + 2 sprigs of thyme.  

*(Optional)* Toss sliced onions, carrot sticks, and halved baby potatoes in a little olive oil, salt, and pepper; spread them across the bottom of each pan. These will caramelize while the chicken roasts.

#### 3️⃣ Arrange & Cook  
- **Single‑batch:** Line a single tray or rack with parchment or foil. Lay all five chickens breast‑upward, spaced slightly apart.  
- **Two‑batch:** Divide evenly between two trays/racks. Keep the first set in the cooler part of the oven (lower shelf); place the second set above when ready.

Preheat oven to **425 °F (220 °C)**.  
Place the tray(s) in the middle of the oven. Roast for **45–55 min per bird**, adjusting for actual weight. Check doneness with a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest thigh bone — target **165 °F (74 °C)**.

> ⚠️ *Always trust the thermometer rather than timing alone.*  

#### 4️⃣ Rest & Serve  
Let each chicken rest uncovered for **10 minutes** after removing from heat. This lets juices redistribute, keeping the meat moist. While resting, let the vegetables finish their last minute of roasting—they’re done when golden brown and tender.

Carve family style or serve individual portions. Pair with fresh salad, crusty bread, or a light vinaigrette.

---

### Quick Tips  

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Use a rack** | Prevents the chicken from sitting in its own fat, ensuring even browning. |
| **High initial heat** | Creates a crispy exterior quickly without drying out the interior. |
| **Rest period** | Juices settle back into the muscle fibers, preventing watery bites. |
| **Check early** | Overcooking leads to tough meat; stop as soon as the thermometer hits 165 °F. |

---

Enjoy your hearty feast! 🍗🥕🍋

Title: Herb-Roasted Chicken – Batch Recipe for Five Chickens

Ingredients:
- 5 whole chickens (about 3‑4 lb each)
- Olive oil
- Salt & black pepper
- Garlic cloves, minced
- Fresh rosemary sprigs
- Thyme leaves
- Lemon halves
- Optional: onion wedges, carrots, potatoes

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
2. Pat chickens dry, season inside/outside with salt/pepper.
3. Stuff cavity with half a lemon, some thyme, rosemary.
4. Rub skin with olive oil, sprinkle garlic, herbs.
5. Place chickens breast-side-up on racks or trays.
6. Roast 45–55 min per chicken depending on size; check internal temp 165°F.
7. Let rest 10 min before carving.
